title: Astrid and the Tide
premise: Vesper Vasquez, a once-celebrated cellist whose hands froze mid-concert in front of a thousand people, retreats to a decaying island inn he's inherited from the grandmother who raised him, intending to sell it before the last ferry of the season. A freak snowstorm traps him there with Halvard Skov, a rival cellist and the man Vesper loved and abandoned a decade ago, and Maren, the inn's stubborn caretaker who knows more about his grandmother's will than she's said. As the storm seals the harbor, Vesper must repair the inn, his grandmother's unfinished cello suite, and the wreckage between himself and Halvard. He ends by choosing to stay: performing his grandmother's final movement on the spring ferry dock, forgiving himself, and beginning again with Halvard rather than selling the past.
about_author: Wren Nystrom is a former orchestral librarian who grew up on ferry schedules and salt air in the northern isles. They write quiet romances about people who mistake discipline for safety.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry Season
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Arriving on the island with a realtor's timeline and a suitcase of avoidance, Vesper surveys the crumbling inn he inherited and resolves to sell fast. Emotional beat: brittle control masking grief over both his grandmother and his ruined career.

chapters.title: Inventory of Broken Things
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Cataloguing the inn's contents, he finds his grandmother's unfinished cello suite and a locked music room. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden; every object accuses him of staying away too long.

chapters.title: Snow Before the Boat
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The caretaker watches the forecast turn vicious and warns Vesper the ferry may not run again until spring. She withholds a letter from the estate file. Emotional beat: quiet defiance and guarded loyalty.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. Snowbound and half-frozen, Halvard arrives seeking shelter after his own retreat from the concert world collapses. The two rivals recognize each other instantly. Emotional beat: shock curdling into hostility.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Forced to share the inn, they negotiate territories like warring nations—kitchen hours, firewood, silence. Emotional beat: old wounds dressed up as house rules.

chapters.title: What the Storm Took
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The power fails; Maren reveals fragments of the grandmother's history and her own debt to her. Emotional beat: three strangers circling one shared loss.

chapters.title: The Heart Is a Muscle
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Alone at night, Vesper tries to play and his hands seize, replaying the catastrophic final performance. Halvard hears him fail. Emotional beat: shame exposed in the dark.

chapters.title: Ten Years Ago, Badly Told
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. Over candlelight, Halvard recounts their shared conservatory past from his side—the competition, the kiss, the abandonment before the biggest audition of their lives. Emotional beat: grievance meeting tenderness.

chapters.title: Chimney Work
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Repairing the chimney together, they fall into wordless rhythm, and Vesper admits he didn't leave out of ambition but terror. Emotional beat: first crack in the armor.

chapters.title: The Locked Music Room
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren finally opens the music room, revealing the grandmother's letters—and evidence that the will's sale clause hinges on conditions Vesper hasn't met. Emotional beat: betrayal and revelation entwined.

chapters.title: Conditions of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Reading the will, Vesper learns he must perform the completed suite publicly to inherit anything at all. He rages at being manipulated from beyond the grave. Emotional beat: fury as fear wearing a coat.

chapters.title: Duet, Reluctantly
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. Halvard offers to rehearse the suite with him—not forgiveness, just musicianship. Their first playing together in a decade is electric and disastrous. Emotional beat: muscle memory outrunning resentment.

chapters.title: Thaw Lines
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A warm spell opens the ice road briefly; Vesper could leave but doesn't, telling himself it's about the will. He and Halvard nearly cross a line neither names. Emotional beat: wanting disguised as hesitation.

chapters.title: Maren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren confesses she stayed silent because the inn was promised to her too, and the will pits them against each other. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: The Mistake of Our Twenties
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. After a near-miss on the ice road nearly kills Vesper, Halvard breaks—admitting he never stopped loving him and that rivalry was the only shape he could give it. Emotional beat: confession as surrender.

chapters.title: One Night, No Promises
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. They spend the night together, tender and terrified, agreeing not to speak of futures. By morning Vesper has already retreated into logistics and ferry timetables. Emotional beat: intimacy followed by self-sabotage.

chapters.title: Hands That Betray
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Rehearsal collapses when Vesper's tremor returns under Halvard's watching eyes; he accuses Halvard of wanting him broken. Emotional beat: love against duty turning inward as war.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Suite
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Deciphering the grandmother's marginalia, Maren realizes the suite itself is a letter—to Vesper, about failure, forgiveness, and the ferry she never took. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into instruction.

chapters.title: Playing It Through
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. Halvard plays the grandmother's unfinished final movement alone so Vesper can hear what he's refusing. Vesper listens from the stairs, undone. Emotional beat: the climax's gathering pressure.

chapters.title: The Mirror in the Music Room
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Alone, Vesper confronts his reflection beside his grandmother's portrait and finally forgives the young man who fled. His hands, for the first time, obey. Emotional beat: internal climax—self-forgiveness.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. On the frozen dock as the season's final ferry sounds its horn, Vesper performs the completed suite for Maren, Halvard, and an audience of gulls—fulfilling the will and himself. Halvard boards or stays? He stays. Emotional beat: public vulnerability rewarded.

chapters.title: Spring, Eventually
chapters.summary: Rotating POV across all three. Weeks later, the inn reopens as a summer music retreat; Maren holds the ledger, Halvard teaches, Vesper plays. Emotional beat: resolution—inheritance redefined as what you choose to carry forward.
